text: For \(3 \times 3\) matrices \(M\) and \(N\), which of the following statement(s) is (are) not correct?
solution: MULTI-KEY (C and D are NOT correct). (a) \(N^T M N\) is symmetric/skew per \(M\): \((N^T M N)^T = N^T M^T N\), so it is symmetric/skew exactly as \(M\) — CORRECT. (b) \(MN - NM\) for symmetric \(M, N\): \((MN-NM)^T = N^T M^T - M^T N^T = NM - MN = -(MN-NM)\) — skew symmetric, CORRECT. (c) \(MN\) symmetric for all symmetric \(M, N\): \((MN)^T = N^T M^T = NM \ne MN\) in general — NOT correct. (d) \((\text{adj} M)(\text{adj} N) = \text{adj}(MN)\): the correct identity is \(\text{adj}(MN) = (\text{adj} N)(\text{adj} M)\), order reversed — NOT correct. Hence the not-correct statements are C and D.

text: If the adjoint of a \(3 \times 3\) matrix \(P\) is \(\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 4 & 4 \\ 2 & 1 & 7 \\ 1 & 1 & 3 \end{pmatrix}\), then the possible value(s) of the determinant of \(P\) is (are)
solution: MULTI-KEY (A and D). \(|\text{adj} P| = |P|^{n-1} = |P|^2\). Compute \(\det\begin{pmatrix} 1 & 4 & 4 \\ 2 & 1 & 7 \\ 1 & 1 & 3 \end{pmatrix} = 4\). So \(|P|^2 = 4\), giving \(|P| = \pm 2\). The possible values are \(-2\) (option A) and \(2\) (option D).

text: Consider the system of equations: \(x + y + z = 0\), \(\alpha x + \beta y + \gamma z = 0\), \(\alpha^2 x + \beta^2 y + \gamma^2 z = 0\). Then the system of equations has
solution: MULTI-KEY (B and C). This homogeneous system has coefficient determinant equal to the Vandermonde determinant \((\beta - \alpha)(\gamma - \alpha)(\gamma - \beta)\). If \(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\) are distinct, the determinant is non-zero, so the only solution is the trivial one (a unique solution) — statement C correct. If any two of \(\alpha, \beta, \gamma\) are equal, the determinant is zero, giving infinitely many solutions — statement B correct. (Option a is wrong since it isn't unique when two are equal; option d is wrong since a homogeneous system never has a finite number \(> 1\) of solutions.)

text: A sphere increases its volume at the rate of \(\pi\ \text{cc/s}\). The rate at which its surface area increases when the radius is 1 cm is
solution: \(V = \frac{4}{3}\pi r^3\), \(\frac{dV}{dt} = 4\pi r^2\frac{dr}{dt} = \pi\). At \(r = 1\): \(4\pi\frac{dr}{dt} = \pi\), so \(\frac{dr}{dt} = \frac{1}{4}\). Then \(S = 4\pi r^2\), \(\frac{dS}{dt} = 8\pi r\frac{dr}{dt} = 8\pi(1)\frac{1}{4} = 2\pi\) sq. cm/s. Hence (A).

text: Let \(f: \left(0, \frac{\pi}{2}\right) \to \mathbb{R}\) be such that \(f(\cos4\theta) = \frac{2}{2-\sec^2\theta}\) for \(\theta \in \left(0, \frac{\pi}{4}\right) \cup \left(\frac{\pi}{4}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right)\). Then the values of \(f\left(\frac{1}{3}\right)\) is (are)
solution: \(f(\cos4\theta) = \frac{2}{2 - \sec^2\theta} = \frac{2\cos^2\theta}{2\cos^2\theta - 1} = \frac{1 + \cos2\theta}{\cos2\theta} = 1 + \frac{1}{\cos2\theta}\). Set \(\cos4\theta = \frac{1}{3}\): \(2\cos^2 2\theta - 1 = \frac{1}{3}\), so \(\cos^2 2\theta = \frac{2}{3}\) and \(\cos2\theta = \pm\sqrt{\frac{2}{3}}\). Therefore \(f\left(\frac{1}{3}\right) = 1 \pm \sqrt{\frac{3}{2}}\), i.e. \(1 - \sqrt{\frac{3}{2}}\) and \(1 + \sqrt{\frac{3}{2}}\). Hence (A) and (B).

text: The value of \(\lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{\sin^2 x + \cos x - 1}{x^2}\) is
solution: For small \(x\): \(\sin^2 x \approx x^2\) and \(\cos x - 1 \approx -\dfrac{x^2}{2}\). So the numerator \(\approx x^2 - \dfrac{x^2}{2} = \dfrac{x^2}{2}\), and \(\dfrac{x^2/2}{x^2} = \dfrac{1}{2}\). Matches option B. Hence (B).

text: The coordinates of a point on the line \(x+y+1=0\) which is at a distance of \(\frac{1}{5}\) unit from the line \(3x+4y+2=0\) are
solution: A point on \(x+y+1=0\) is \((t,-1-t)\). Its distance from \(3x+4y+2=0\) is \(\frac{|3t+4(-1-t)+2|}{5}=\frac{|-t-2|}{5}=\frac15\Rightarrow |t+2|=1\Rightarrow t=-1\) or \(t=-3\), giving \((-1,0)\) and \((-3,2)\). Both options (B) and (D) satisfy the condition; the keyed answer is (B).

[Textbook note: the source book keys option A (0) and its printed solution reaches 0 via a sign error in the left-hand difference quotient; the correct value is 1.]

text: Let Z be the set of integers. Then the relation \(R = \{(a, b) : 1 + ab > 0\}\) defined on Z is
solution: \(R=\{(a,b):1+ab>0\}\) on Z. Reflexive (\(1+a^2>0\)); symmetric (\(1+ab=1+ba\)); NOT transitive (\(a=2,b=0,c=-2\): \(1+0>0,\ 1+0>0\), but \(1+ac=1-4=-3\not>0\)). So reflexive and symmetric but not transitive. Hence (C). [Textbook note: the source book keys option D ('equivalence relation'), but transitivity fails on Z (a=2, b=0, c=−2), so the relation is reflexive and symmetric but not transitive.]

text: If \(\log_k x \cdot \log_5 k = \log_x 5\), \(k \neq 1\), \(k > 0\), then \(x\) is equal to
solution: \(\log_k x \cdot \log_5 k = \log_5 x\) (change of base), so \(\log_5 x = \log_x 5 = \dfrac{1}{\log_5 x}\), giving \((\log_5 x)^2 = 1\), i.e. \(\log_5 x = \pm 1\). Hence \(x = 5\) or \(x = \dfrac15\).

text: For two events A and B, \(P(A) = 0.7\) and \(P(B) = 0.6\). The necessarily false statement(s) is/are
solution: By the bounds \(\max(0, P(A)+P(B)-1) \le P(A \cap B) \le \min(P(A), P(B))\), here \(0.3 \le P(A \cap B) \le 0.6\). So \(0.35\) and \(0.45\) are possible, while \(0.65 > 0.6\) and \(0.28 < 0.3\) are impossible. The necessarily false statements are (C) and (D).

text: Let X and Y be two events such that \(P(X) = \dfrac{1}{3}\), \(P(X \mid Y) = \dfrac{1}{2}\) and \(P(Y \mid X) = \dfrac{2}{5}\). Then
solution: \(P(X \cap Y) = P(Y \mid X)P(X) = \dfrac{2}{5} \times \dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac{2}{15}\). Then \(P(Y) = \dfrac{P(X \cap Y)}{P(X \mid Y)} = \dfrac{2/15}{1/2} = \dfrac{4}{15}\) (statement C is true). Also \(P(X' \mid Y) = 1 - P(X \mid Y) = \dfrac{1}{2}\) (statement B is true). \(P(X \cap Y) = \dfrac{2}{15} \ne \dfrac{2}{5}\) and \(P(X \cup Y) = \dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{4}{15} - \dfrac{2}{15} = \dfrac{7}{15} \ne \dfrac{2}{5}\). Correct: B and C.

text: Let X and Y be two events such that \(P(X \mid Y) = \dfrac{1}{2}\), \(P(Y \mid X) = \dfrac{1}{3}\) and \(P(X \cap Y) = \dfrac{1}{6}\). Which of the following is(are) correct?
solution: \(P(Y) = \dfrac{P(X \cap Y)}{P(X \mid Y)} = \dfrac{1/6}{1/2} = \dfrac{1}{3}\) and \(P(X) = \dfrac{P(X \cap Y)}{P(Y \mid X)} = \dfrac{1/6}{1/3} = \dfrac{1}{2}\). Then \(P(X \cup Y) = \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{3} - \dfrac{1}{6} = \dfrac{2}{3}\) (A true). Also \(P(X)P(Y) = \dfrac{1}{6} = P(X \cap Y)\), so X and Y are independent (B true). Correct: A and B.

text: Let E and F be two independent events. The probability that exactly one of them occurs is \(\dfrac{11}{25}\) and the probability of none of them occurring is \(\dfrac{2}{25}\). If P(T) denotes the probability of occurrence of the event T, then
solution: Let \(e = P(E)\), \(f = P(F)\), independent. \((1-e)(1-f) = \dfrac{2}{25}\) and \(e + f - 2ef = \dfrac{11}{25}\). Solving gives \(\{e, f\} = \left\{\dfrac{4}{5}, \dfrac{3}{5}\right\}\), so both \((P(E),P(F)) = \left(\dfrac{4}{5}, \dfrac{3}{5}\right)\) and \(\left(\dfrac{3}{5}, \dfrac{4}{5}\right)\) are valid. Correct: A and D.

text: Let OA = a, OB = b and if the vector along the angle bisector of ∠AOB is given by x(a/|a|) + y(b/|b|), then
solution: Angle bisector direction is proportional to a/|a|+b/|b|, so x=y, i.e. x-y=0.

text: The value of α, so that the volume of the parallelepiped formed by i+αj+k, j+αk and αi+k becomes maximum, is
A relation \(\rho\) on the set of real numbers R is defined as follows: '\(x \rho y\) if and only if \(xy > 0\)'. Then which on the following is/are true?
solution: \(x \rho y\) iff \(xy > 0\). Reflexive fails at \(x = 0\) (\(0 \cdot 0 = 0 \not> 0\)), so not reflexive on all of R. Symmetric: \(xy > 0 \Leftrightarrow yx > 0\), yes. Transitive: if \(xy > 0\) and \(yz > 0\) (both nonzero, same sign through y) then \(xz > 0\), yes. So it is symmetric but not reflexive (B) and symmetric and transitive (C). Both B and C are correct. Hence (B, C).
